newsitem.title: ARMENIA: New Armenian premier vows to stick to reform.
newsitem.headline: New Armenian premier vows to stick to reform.

text.p: Armenia's new prime minister, Armen Sarkisyan, said on Tuesday he would follow his predecessor in pushing forward economic reform and defending the independence of the former Soviet republic in the Caucasus.

"The new government will continue the course of social and economic reforms...and will also continue the successful work of the previous government," Sarkisyan, 43, told parliament in his maiden policy speech.

Sarkisyan's predecessor, Grant Bagratyan, oversaw three and a half years of wrenching economic reforms after the breakup of the Soviet Union against the background of Armenia's bitter conflict with Azerbaijan.

Bagratyan became a lightning rod for opposition groups who said that reforms had been too drastic and benefited too few people, but was credited by organisations like the International Monetary Fund and World Bank with taking the bold steps needed to start to get the economy back on track.
Sarkisyan described the landlocked country's post-Soviet years as a "fight for survival".
"We should enter the 21st century so that regional economic and political forces cannot swallow our state," he said.
Sarkisyan did not specify what forces he meant.
Bagratyan resigned on Monday in a clear attempt to soothe public feeling after the controversial re-election of President Levon Ter-Petrosyan six weeks ago.
Ter-Petrosyan sent tanks on to the streets of the capital Yerevan and briefly arrested dozens of political opponents after demonstrations accusing him of vote-rigging turned violent.

The Central Electoral Commission said he took 51.8 percent to 41.3 percent for another former prime minister, Vazgen Manukyan. But the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said major violations marred voting.
